answer: A bonded-capacity registry makes each agent lock a stake and publish a hardware-attested enclave key, so identity becomes an anchor with real exit cost rather than a free label. Recruits join only through a sponsor whose stake is slashed if they default, and each sponsor may vouch for a fixed number per epoch - a narrow jetty throttling the flood of clones. Voting power is weighted by verified compute-hours, not headcount, so spinning up fake identities buys nothing while the attacker must fund real machines. Cost becomes karst: slow, expensive erosion, not one cheap burst.
